questions.subject: english
questions.content: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: For third person singular in simple present tense, we add -es to go.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: They ___ football on Sundays.
questions.explanation: With plural subject 'they' in simple present tense, use the base form 'play'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: He ___ a cake yesterday.
questions.explanation: Yesterday indicates simple past tense. 'Ate' is the past form of eat.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We ___ to the park last week.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' indicates past time. 'Went' is the past form of go.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: I ___ visit my grandma tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' indicates future time. Use 'will' for simple future tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: It ___ rain this afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'This afternoon' (future context) uses 'will' for future tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Look! The cat ___ on the sofa.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' indicates action happening now. Use present continuous: is + verb-ing.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Listen! The birds ___ in the tree.
questions.explanation: 'Listen!' indicates action happening now. Use present continuous: are + verb-ing.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: My birthday is ___ July.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' for months and years.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We have class ___ 8 o'clock.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for specific clock times.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences are in simple present tense? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'He plays' and 'She reads' are simple present tense. 'Went' is past tense. 'Are happy' is present simple (state verb).

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which prepositions can fill the blank? 'The book is ___ the table.' (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'On the table' and 'under the table' are both correct spatial prepositions.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which words are past tense verbs? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Went (go), ate (eat), and saw (see) are past tense forms.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences use present continuous tense? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Present continuous uses am/is/are + verb-ing. 'Eats' is simple present.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: She often ___ (watch) TV in the evening.
questions.explanation: For third person singular in simple present tense, add -es to watch.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Yesterday they ___ (play) basketball.
questions.explanation: Yesterday indicates past tense. Add -ed to play for regular past form.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Tomorrow I ___ (go) to Beijing.
questions.explanation: Tomorrow indicates future tense. Use will + base verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We play games ___ the playground.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for surfaces like playground.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Look! The dog ___ (run) after the ball.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' indicates action now. Present continuous: is + running.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'He go to school every day.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Third person singular requires 'goes', not 'go'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'My birthday is on Monday.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Correct. We use 'on' for days of the week.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'They are play games now.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Incorrect. Present continuous requires 'playing', not 'play'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Write 3 sentences about what you did yesterday. Use simple past tense.
questions.correct_answer: Sample: I woke up at 7. I ate breakfast. I went to school.
questions.explanation: Use simple past tense verbs like woke, ate, went, played, studied.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: The sun ___ in the east.
questions.explanation: The sun rising is a universal truth, so we use simple present tense with -es for third person.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: She ___ her homework last night.
questions.explanation: 'Last night' indicates past tense. 'Did' is the past form of do.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Look at the clouds. It ___ rain.
questions.explanation: When we see evidence now, we use 'be going to' for future predictions.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We ___ a party next Saturday.
questions.explanation: Present continuous can express definite future plans.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: I was born ___ 2014.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' for years.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We have lunch ___ noon.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for noon, midnight, and specific times.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: The meeting is ___ Monday morning.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for specific days and day parts (Monday morning).

questions.subject: english
questions.content: He ___ his leg last month.
questions.explanation: 'Last month' indicates past tense. 'Broke' is the past form of break.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: He usually ___ coffee, but today he ___ tea.
questions.explanation: 'Usually' indicates habit (simple present). 'Today' indicates current exception (present continuous).

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Read the passage: 'Tom woke up early. He put on his uniform and went to school. At school, he met his best friend Jack.' Where did Tom meet Jack?
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states 'At school, he met his best friend Jack.'

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences are in simple past tense? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Walked, played, and watched are past tense verbs. 'Eats' is present tense.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences use 'in' correctly? (Select all that apply)
options: A. I was born in May.
B. We play in the morning.
C. The meeting is in Monday.
questions.explanation: 'In' is correct for months, morning/afternoon/evening, and cities. Days use 'on'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences are grammatically correct? (Select all that apply)
options: D. We will visit grandma tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'He go' is incorrect; it should be 'He goes' or 'He went'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Read the passage: 'It was a hot summer day. The sun was shining brightly. Children were playing in the pool.' Which words describe the weather? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Hot, summer, and shining describe weather conditions. 'Playing' describes activity.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Water ___ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific facts use simple present tense. Third person singular adds -s.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Last summer, we ___ (swim) in the sea.
questions.explanation: 'Last summer' indicates past tense. 'Swam' is the past form of swim.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Next year, my sister ___ (be) 12 years old.
questions.explanation: 'Next year' indicates future. Use will + be.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Please put the books ___ the shelf.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' for surfaces.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Be quiet! The baby ___ (sleep) now.
questions.explanation: 'Now' indicates present continuous: is + sleeping.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'She is liking apples.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: 'Like' is a stative verb and is not normally used in continuous tenses.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'We met him in the library yesterday.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Met' is past tense, and 'in the library' uses correct preposition.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'The concert is on Friday evening.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Correct. We use 'on' for specific days and day parts.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Describe your best friend using 3-5 sentences. Include what he/she looks like and what he/she likes to do.
questions.correct_answer: Sample: My best friend is tall. She has long hair. She likes reading books. We play together every day.
questions.explanation: Use simple present tense for descriptions and habits.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Write what you are going to do this weekend. Use 'be going to' in your answer.
questions.correct_answer: Sample: I am going to visit my grandparents. I am going to play basketball with my brother.
questions.explanation: Use am/is/are going to + verb for future plans.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: When I called, he ___ a shower.
questions.explanation: Past continuous describes an action in progress when another action interrupted it.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: This time tomorrow, we ___ on the train to Paris.
questions.explanation: Future continuous (will be + verb-ing) describes an action in progress at a specific future time.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: I ___ this book before.
questions.explanation: Present perfect (have + past participle) connects past action to present experience.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: The picture is ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: Pictures hang on the surface of walls, so we use 'on'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We will leave ___ the morning of July 20th.
questions.explanation: When morning/afternoon/evening has a specific date, use 'on'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: He said he ___ come to the party tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, will changes to would.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Read the passage: 'The old man sat on a bench in the park. He watched the children playing. A little girl came up and gave him a flower. He smiled and thanked her.' What is the main idea of this passage?
options: A. Children like to play in the park.
B. An old man received kindness from a child.
C. Flowers grow in the park.
D. Old people like sitting on benches.
questions.explanation: The passage centers on the interaction where a girl gives a flower to an old man.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: She is interested ___ learning French.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'interested in'.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: The train ___ at 6 PM every day.
questions.explanation: Timetabled events use simple present tense for future meaning.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Read the passage: 'Maya loved drawing. Every day after school, she drew pictures of animals. Her favorite animal was the elephant. She drew big ears and long trunks.' What was Maya's favorite animal?
questions.explanation: The passage states 'Her favorite animal was the elephant.'

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences use future tense? (Select all that apply)
options: A. I will call you later.
B. She is going to study medicine.
questions.explanation: Will, be going to, and present simple for timetables all express future. 'Are playing' is present continuous.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which prepositions can fill the blank? 'The shop is ___ the corner of Main Street.' (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Both 'on the corner' (American English) and 'at the corner' (British English) are acceptable.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Read the passage: 'Tom and Lily went camping. They set up a tent near a lake. At night, they saw many stars. They cooked fish over a fire.' Which statements are true? (Select all that apply)
options: A. They stayed in a hotel.
C. They saw stars at night.
questions.explanation: They set up a tent (not hotel), near a lake, saw stars, and cooked fish.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Which sentences are grammatically correct? (Select all that apply)
options: A. She has lived here since 2020.
B. I have seen that movie twice.
C. They are being very quiet.
D. He will have finished by 5 PM.
questions.explanation: All four sentences use advanced tenses correctly: present perfect, present perfect, present continuous with 'being', future perfect.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: While I ___ (walk) home, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: Past continuous for ongoing action when another action (started) interrupted.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: I ___ never ___ (be) to Paris.
questions.explanation: Present perfect: have/has + been (past participle of be).

questions.subject: english
questions.content: The ball rolled ___ the door and stopped.
questions.explanation: 'Under' indicates movement to a position beneath something.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: If it ___ (not rain), we will go hiking.
questions.explanation: In first conditional, use simple present in the if-clause.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: We arrived ___ the airport two hours early.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' for specific points/locations like airports.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'I have seen that movie last week.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Present perfect cannot be used with specific past time expressions like 'last week'. Use simple past: 'I saw that movie last week.'

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'She sat beside me during the lesson.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Beside' means next to, and simple past 'sat' is correct for a completed action.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: 'The shop is between the bank and the post office.' Is this sentence correct?
questions.explanation: Correct. 'Between' is used when something is in the middle of two things.

questions.subject: english
questions.content: Look at the picture description: A boy is helping an old lady cross the street. Write 4-6 sentences describing what happened. Use past tense.
questions.correct_answer: Sample: Yesterday, Tom saw an old lady at the crosswalk. She looked worried. He walked over and offered his hand. He helped her cross the street slowly. The old lady smiled and thanked him. Tom felt very happy.
questions.explanation: Use simple past tense for the main events and past continuous for background actions.
